tools.whois-lookup.faqs.0.question: What is Whois?
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.0.answer: Whois is the protocol for looking up domain registration data. This tool uses its modern standard, RDAP, to return the registrar, creation/expiry dates, domain status and DNS servers.
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.1.question: Why can't I see the registrant's name and email?
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.1.answer: Since the GDPR took effect in 2018, most registrars redact the registrant contact details of personal domains. Only the registrar, dates, status and DNS servers remain public.
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.2.question: Which TLDs are supported?
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.2.answer: Via the rdap.org bootstrap service, most gTLDs (.com, .net, .org, .io and more) and many ccTLDs (.cn, .jp, .de, .uk and more) are supported. A few TLDs without RDAP may return partial data.
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.3.question: How fresh is the data?
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.3.answer: RDAP queries each registry's authoritative data source directly, returning real-time (or registry-cached) information.
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.4.question: Is it free and safe?
tools.whois-lookup.faqs.4.answer: Completely free. Your browser queries the public RDAP service directly; domain registration data is public information, with no sign-up or API key required.

tools.ip-lookup.faqs.0.question: What is an IP address lookup?
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.0.answer: An IP address lookup uses RDAP (Registration Data Access Protocol) to view the network an IP belongs to: CIDR block, owner, country/region, network type and status.
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.1.question: How do I see my public IP?
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.1.answer: Open the tool and it automatically detects and displays your public IP and its network information. Click Refresh to re-detect.
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.2.question: Does it support IPv6?
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.2.answer: RDAP supports both IPv4 and IPv6. The current input box accepts IPv4 format; IPv6 lookup is being improved.
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.3.question: How accurate are the results?
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.3.answer: Data comes from the official RDAP services of the five Regional Internet Registries (ARIN, RIPE, APNIC, LACNIC, AFRINIC) — authoritative network allocation information.
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.4.question: Is it free and safe?
tools.ip-lookup.faqs.4.answer: Completely free. Your browser queries the public RDAP service directly — no sign-up, no API key.

tools.binary-converter.faqs.0.question: What is a binary converter?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.0.answer: A binary converter is a tool that converts numbers between binary (base 2), decimal (base 10), hexadecimal (base 16), and octal (base 8).
tools.binary-converter.faqs.1.question: How do I convert numbers?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.1.answer: Enter a number in the input field. Select the base of the number you entered. The tool automatically converts it to all other bases and displays the results.
tools.binary-converter.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between binary and decimal?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.2.answer: Binary uses base 2 (only the digits 0 and 1), while decimal uses base 10 (digits 0-9). Binary is used in computing; decimal is used for everyday counting.
tools.binary-converter.faqs.3.question: What is hexadecimal?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.3.answer: Hexadecimal is a base 16 number system using digits 0-9 and letters A-F. It is commonly used in computing to represent color codes, memory addresses, and other values.
tools.binary-converter.faqs.4.question: What is octal?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.4.answer: Octal is a base 8 number system using digits 0-7. It is sometimes used in computing, particularly for Unix permissions.
tools.binary-converter.faqs.5.question: Is the converter safe?
tools.binary-converter.faqs.5.answer: Yes. This tool converts numbers locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server.

tools.pregnancy-calculator.faqs.0.questi: How is the due date calculated?
tools.pregnancy-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Using Naegele's rule: add 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP). This assumes a 28-day cycle - the calculator adjusts for different cycle lengths.
tools.pregnancy-calculator.faqs.1.questi: Is the due date calculator accurate?
tools.pregnancy-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Only about 4% of babies are born on their exact due date. Most are born within 2 weeks of it. The due date is an estimate - healthcare providers may adjust it based on ultrasound measurements.
tools.pregnancy-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Conception typically occurs about 14 days after the first day of your last period (at ovulation). This adjusts with cycle length - longer cycles mean later ovulation.

tools.pace-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate pace?
tools.pace-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Pace = time ÷ distance. If you run 3.1 miles in 25 minutes: 25 ÷ 3.1 = 8:04/mile pace. For kilometers, divide by the distance in kilometers instead.
tools.pace-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is a good running pace?
tools.pace-calculator.faqs.1.answer: It varies widely. Beginners: 10-13 minutes/mile. Intermediate: 8-10 minutes/mile. Advanced: 6-8 minutes/mile. Elite: under 5 minutes/mile. Focus on personal progress, not comparisons.
tools.pace-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I convert pace to speed?
tools.pace-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Speed (mph) = 60 ÷ pace (minutes per mile). An 8:00/mile pace = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 mph. An 8:00/km pace = 7.5 km/h.

tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is BMR?
tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Basal metabolic rate is the number of calories your body needs at complete rest to maintain basic functions like breathing, circulation, and cell production. It typically accounts for 60-75% of daily energy expenditure.
tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.1.question: Which BMR formula is best?
tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Mifflin-St Jeor is considered the most accurate for most people. Harris-Benedict tends to slightly overestimate. If you know your body fat percentage, Katch-McArdle is best.
tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.2.question: How is BMR different from TDEE?
tools.bmr-calculator.faqs.2.answer: BMR is calories at rest. TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) = BMR × activity factor. TDEE includes all daily activity and exercise. Use TDEE for calorie planning, not BMR alone.

tools.waist-to-hip-ratio-calculator.faqs: Waist-to-hip ratio = waist circumference ÷ hip circumference. It measures fat distribution. Higher ratios (more abdominal fat) are associated with increased health risks for heart disease, diabetes, and stroke.
What is a healthy waist-to-hip ratio?
WHO guidelines: men should stay below 0.90 and women below 0.80. Ratios above 1.0 (men) or 0.85 (women) indicate significantly elevated health risk.
Waist: measure at the narrowest point between the ribs and hip bones (usually at the navel). Hips: measure at the widest part of the buttocks. Keep the tape horizontal, snug but not tight.

tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.0.que: How much water should I drink per day?
tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.0.ans: A general guideline is about 35 ml per kilogram of body weight (roughly half your weight in ounces). Active people and those in hot climates need more. The '8 glasses of water a day' rule is a rough estimate.
tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.1.que: Does coffee count toward my water intake?
tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.1.ans: Mostly yes. Although caffeine is a mild diuretic, the water in coffee and tea still contributes to hydration. However, plain water remains the best source.
tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.2.que: How do I know if I'm well hydrated?
tools.water-intake-calculator.faqs.2.ans: Check your urine color — pale yellow indicates good hydration. Dark yellow means you need to drink more water. Other signs of dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, headache, and fatigue.

tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is a 1RM?
tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Your one-rep max (1RM) is the maximum weight you can lift with proper form. It is used to set training percentages and track strength progress.
tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.1.question: Which 1RM formula is most accurate?
tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Brzycki and Epley are the most commonly used and tend to be accurate for 1-10 reps. All formulas become less accurate above 10 reps. For best accuracy, test with a weight you can lift 3-5 times.
tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I train using my 1RM?
tools.1rm-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Common training zones: Strength: 80-90%, 3-5 reps. Hypertrophy: 65-80%, 8-12 reps. Endurance: 50-65%, 15-20 reps. Power: 50-70%, 3-6 explosive reps.

tools.annuity-calculator.metadata.title: Annuity Calculator
tools.annuity-calculator.metadata.descri: Calculate the present and future value of an annuity, supporting ordinary and annuity due.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is an annuity and how does it work?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.0.answer: An annuity is a financial contract between you and an insurance company. During the accumulation phase, you invest money that grows tax-deferred. During the payout (annuitization) phase, the insurer pays you a regular income stream. Annuities are commonly used for retirement planning to guarantee income you cannot outlive.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between a fixed and variable annuity?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.1.answer: A fixed annuity offers a guaranteed interest rate and predictable growth, making it lower risk. A variable annuity invests in sub-accounts similar to mutual funds, so returns fluctuate with the market. Variable annuities have higher growth potential but also more risk. This calculator models both so you can compare projected outcomes.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.2.question: How does tax-deferred growth benefit an annuity?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.2.answer: In a tax-deferred annuity, you don't pay taxes on investment gains each year. This lets your entire balance compound without tax drag. Over decades, this advantage can be substantial. For example, at a 6% return and 25% tax rate over 20 years, tax deferral can result in tens of thousands of dollars more in your account compared to a taxable investment.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.3.question: How is my annuity payout amount calculated?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Payout amounts are calculated using the present value of an annuity formula: PMT = PV x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), where PV is your account balance, r is the interest rate per period, and n is the total number of payment periods. This ensures your balance is fully distributed over the chosen payout period while continuing to earn interest.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.4.question: When should I consider buying an annuity?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Annuities are worth considering if you've maxed out other tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA), want guaranteed retirement income, or are concerned about outliving your savings. They work best as part of a diversified retirement strategy. Deferred annuities are most effective when purchased 10-30 years before retirement to maximize tax-deferred compounding.
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.5.question: What fees are typically associated with annuities?
tools.annuity-calculator.faqs.5.answer: Common annuity fees include mortality and expense charges (1-1.5%), administrative fees, fund management fees for variable annuities (0.5-2%), and surrender charges for early withdrawal (typically 5-10% declining over 5-10 years). This calculator shows gross returns before fees. Subtract roughly 1-2.5% from the interest rate to estimate after-fee performance for variable annuities.

Estimate blood alcohol concentration (BAC) based on drinks, weight, gender, and time.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.0.qu: How does the Widmark formula calculate BAC?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.0.an: The Widmark formula estimates BAC as: BAC = (grams of alcohol consumed / (body weight in grams x Widmark r factor)) - (0.015 x hours since first drink). The Widmark r factor accounts for differences in body water distribution between genders (0.68 for men, 0.55 for women). The 0.015 rate represents the average hourly elimination rate of alcohol.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.1.qu: What is a standard drink in the U.S.?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.1.an: A U.S. standard drink contains about 14 grams (0.6 fluid ounces) of pure alcohol. This is roughly equivalent to 12 ounces of regular beer (5% ABV), 5 ounces of wine (12% ABV), or 1.5 ounces of distilled spirits (40% ABV / 80 proof). Many cocktails and craft beers contain more than one standard drink.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.2.an: This calculator provides only a rough estimate. Actual BAC is influenced by many factors not considered here, including food intake, medications, liver health, hydration status, individual metabolism, genetics, and body composition. Two people of the same weight and gender can have very different BACs after drinking the same amount. Never rely on a calculator to judge whether it is safe to drive.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.3.qu: What BAC level is considered drunk driving?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.3.an: In the U.S., the legal driving limit for drivers aged 21 and over in all 50 states is 0.08% BAC. Commercial drivers (CDL holders) have a lower limit of 0.04%. Drivers under 21 face zero-tolerance laws, typically 0.00-0.02% depending on the state. Many countries have lower limits, such as 0.05% in Australia and most of Europe.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.4.qu: How long does alcohol take to leave the body?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.4.an: On average, the body eliminates alcohol at a rate of about 0.015% BAC per hour, roughly equal to one standard drink per hour. However, this rate varies from person to person. A person with a BAC of 0.08% would need about 5.3 hours to reach 0.00%. There is no way to speed up the process; coffee, cold showers, and exercise will not lower BAC faster.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.5.qu: Why does body weight affect BAC?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.5.an: Alcohol distributes through body water. Larger people typically have more body water to dilute the alcohol, resulting in a lower BAC for the same amount of alcohol. This is also why the Widmark factor differs by gender: men generally have a higher body water percentage (68%) than women (55%), meaning the same amount of alcohol at the same weight typically produces a higher BAC in women.
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.6.qu: Can I use this calculator to know if it is safe to drive?
tools.blood-alcohol-calculator.faqs.6.an: No. This calculator is for educational and informational purposes only. The rough estimate it provides can differ significantly from your actual BAC. Impairment can occur even below legal limits. The only safe amount of alcohol to consume before driving is zero. If you have been drinking, use a designated driver, ride-share service, or taxi.

tools.calorie-deficit-calculator.metadat: Calculate how many calories to eat per day for weight loss based on your TDEE.
A calorie deficit means consuming fewer calories than your body burns (TDEE). A daily deficit of 500 calories can lead to about 1 pound of fat loss per week (3,500 calories = 1 pound).
How large should the deficit be?

A 500-calorie daily deficit (1 pound per week) is sustainable for most people. Deficits over 1,000 calories per day may lead to muscle loss, fatigue, and a slowed metabolism. Don't go below 1,200 calories per day without medical supervision.
Why am I not losing weight despite a deficit?

Common causes: underestimating portion sizes, not tracking cooking oils or drinks, water retention masking fat loss, or metabolic adaptation. Try accurately re-measuring your food intake for 1-2 weeks.

tools.car-lease-calculator.metadata.desc: Calculate monthly lease payments, money factor, and total lease cost.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.0.questi: What is a money factor in car leasing?
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.0.answer: The money factor is the lease equivalent of an interest rate, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0025). To convert to APR, multiply by 2,400. A lower money factor means lower financing costs.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.1.questi: How is the monthly lease payment calculated?
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Monthly lease payment = (Depreciation + Rent Charge) × Tax. Depreciation = (Negotiated Price - Residual Value) / Term. Rent Charge = (Negotiated Price + Residual Value) × Money Factor.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Residual value is the estimated worth of the vehicle at lease end, set by the leasing company. It's typically 50-60% of MSRP for a 3-year lease. Higher residual means lower monthly payments.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Leasing is better if you drive less than 15,000 miles/year, want lower monthly payments, and prefer driving a new car every 2-3 years. Buying is better if you drive a lot, plan to keep the car long-term, or want to build equity.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.4.questi: Can I negotiate the lease price?
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. The negotiated price (cap cost) is negotiable just like a purchase price. Lower negotiated price means lower monthly payments. Research invoice prices and negotiate before discussing lease terms.
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.5.questi: What fees are included in a lease?
tools.car-lease-calculator.faqs.5.answer: Typical lease fees include acquisition fee, disposition fee, excess mileage charges, and wear-and-tear fees. This calculator focuses on monthly payments. Ask the dealer for a complete fee breakdown.
